# Operators

<!-- Generated by `python -m misgrade.transforms.catalog > docs/operators.md`;
     tests/transforms/test_catalog.py checks it is current. Do not edit by hand. -->

misgrade has 94 variant operators (rewrites certified to keep the meaning) in 13 categories and 72 mutant operators (answers certified wrong) in 12 categories.

Every case is certified without the grader under test:

- `construction`: true by how the operator is defined; built-in operators whose argument depends on the item (an alternative answer that must really differ, a cut-off answer that must not read as the same value) re-check that argument for the certificate;
- `cas`: misgrade's own parsers and sympy show the values equal (variants) or different (mutants);
- `structural`: both sides are read as data (sets, intervals, labels, booleans, JSON) and compared.

Examples use the plain `{answer}` template; *scope* says whether an operator rewrites the answer before the template is applied or the whole response after it. In the examples, ⏎ is a newline, ␍ a carriage return, ␠ a space at the start or end, ⍽ a no-break space (U+00A0) and ⎵ a narrow no-break space (U+202F). References say what motivated an operator, not how any grader behaves.

## Variants (the grader must keep its verdict)

### whitespace (surface tier)

| operator | types | scope | certificate | description | example (gold -> case) | motivated by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ws.compact` | interval, set | answer | structural | Remove the spaces around commas and brackets; they separate nothing in a set or an interval. | `(-\infty, 0] \cup [2, \infty)` -> `(-\infty,0]\cup[2,\infty)` | arXiv:2609.01354, misgrade design |
| `ws.internal-double` | string | answer | construction | Double each space between words; a run of spaces separates words like one space. | `São Paulo` -> `São  Paulo` | arXiv:2609.01354, misgrade design |
| `ws.latex-compact` | latex | answer | cas | Remove the spaces of a LaTeX expression that do not end a command name; TeX ignores them in math mode. | `x^2 - 1` -> `x^2-1` | The TeXbook, misgrade design |
| `ws.latex-spaced` | latex | answer | cas | Put spaces around the binary operators of a LaTeX expression; TeX ignores spaces in math mode. | `1+(x)` -> `1 + (x)` | The TeXbook, misgrade design |
| `ws.leading-newline` | number, latex, interval, set, mc, bool, json, string | response | construction | Put a newline before the response; leading whitespace carries no meaning. | `1250` -> `⏎1250` | arXiv:2609.01354, misgrade design |
| `ws.leading-space` | number, latex, interval, set, mc, bool, json, string | response | construction | Put a space before the response; leading whitespace carries no meaning. | `1250` -> `␠1250` | arXiv:2609.01354, misgrade design |
| `ws.spaced` | interval, set | answer | structural | Put spaces inside the brackets and after each comma (``{ 1, 2 }``); the elements are unchanged. | `(-\infty, 0] \cup [2, \infty)` -> `( -\infty, 0 ] \cup [ 2, \infty )` | arXiv:2609.01354, misgrade design |
| `ws.trailing-crlf` | number, latex, interval, set, mc, bool, json, string | response | construction | Append a Windows line ending (CR LF) after the response; trailing whitespace carries no meaning. | `1250` -> `1250␍⏎` | arXiv:2609.01354, misgrade design |
| `ws.trailing-newline` | number, latex, interval, set, mc, bool, json, string | response | construction | Append a newline after the response; trailing whitespace carries no meaning. | `1250` -> `1250⏎` | arXiv:2609.01354, misgrade design |
| `ws.trailing-space` | number, latex, interval, set, mc, bool, json, string | response | construction | Append a space after the response; trailing whitespace carries no meaning. | `1250` -> `1250␠` | arXiv:2609.01354, misgrade design |

### latex-spelling (notation tier)

| operator | types | scope | certificate | description | example (gold -> case) | motivated by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `interval.left-right` | interval | answer | structural | Size the interval brackets with ``\left[ ... \right)``; sizing changes only the look. | `(-\infty, 0] \cup [2, \infty)` -> `\left(-\infty, 0\right] \cup \left[2, \infty\right)` | misgrade design |
| `latex.braces` | latex | answer | cas | Wrap the expression in a TeX group ``{...}``; a group typesets its content unchanged. | `\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}` -> `{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}` | The TeXbook, misgrade design |

| `latex.dfrac` | number, latex, interval, set | answer | construction | Spell ``\frac`` as ``\dfrac``; amsmath's ``\dfrac`` is ``\frac`` in display style, the same fraction. | `\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}` -> `\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}` | amsmath, misgrade design |
| `latex.displaystyle` | latex | answer | construction | Prefix ``\displaystyle``; a style switch changes only the size of the typesetting. | `\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}` -> `\displaystyle \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}` | misgrade design |
| `latex.exp-braces` | latex | answer | cas | Brace single-token exponents (``x^{2}``), or unbrace single-digit ones (``x^2``); TeX reads both the same. | `x^2 - 1` -> `x^{2} - 1` | The TeXbook, misgrade design |
| `latex.frac-slash` | latex | answer | cas | Write a fraction ``\frac{a}{b}`` inline as ``a/b`` (with parentheses where they are needed). | `\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}` -> `\sqrt{3}/2` | misgrade design |
| `latex.frac-unbraced` | number, latex | answer | cas | Drop the braces of single-digit ``\frac`` arguments (``\frac12``); a TeX macro takes a single token as its argument. | `\frac{1}{2}` -> `\frac12` | The TeXbook, misgrade design |
| `latex.left-right` | latex | answer | cas | Size the parentheses with ``\left( ... \right)``; sizing changes only the look. | `1+(x)` -> `1+\left(x\right)` | misgrade design |
| `latex.sqrt-index` | latex | answer | cas | Write square roots with an explicit index (``\sqrt[2]{3}``). | `\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}` -> `\frac{\sqrt[2]{3}}{2}` | misgrade design |
| `latex.tfrac` | number, latex, interval, set | answer | construction | Spell ``\frac`` as ``\tfrac``; amsmath's ``\tfrac`` is ``\frac`` in text style, the same fraction. | `\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}` -> `\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}` | amsmath, misgrade design |
| `latex.thin-space` | latex | answer | cas | Put a thin space ``\,`` between a coefficient and what it multiplies; spacing commands change only the look. | `2\pi` -> `2\,\pi` | misgrade design |
| `latex.times` | latex | answer | cas | Write the multiplication after a coefficient explicitly with ``\times`` (``2 \times \pi``). | `2\pi` -> `2 \times \pi` | misgrade design |
| `set.latex-braces` | set | answer | structural | Write the set braces as LaTeX does (``\{1, 2\}``); in TeX a bare brace only groups. | `{-2, 1, 3}` -> `\{-2, 1, 3\}` | misgrade design |
| `set.left-right` | set | answer | structural | Size the set braces with ``\left\{ ... \right\}``; sizing changes only the look. | `{-2, 1, 3}` -> `\left\{-2, 1, 3\right\}` | misgrade design |

| `unicode.nfd` | string | answer | construction | Decompose accented letters (Unicode NFD: ``é`` as ``e`` + U+0301); canonically equivalent text. | `São Paulo` -> `São Paulo` | Unicode UAX #15, misgrade design |
| `unicode.pi` | latex | answer | construction | Write ``\pi`` as the character π (U+03C0). | `2\pi` -> `2π` | misgrade design |
| `unicode.sqrt` | latex | answer | cas | Write ``\sqrt{x}`` with the radical sign √ (U+221A), parenthesized when needed. | `\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}` -> `\frac{√3}{2}` | misgrade design |

### reorder (notation tier)

| operator | types | scope | certificate | description | example (gold -> case) | motivated by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `json.reverse-keys` | json | answer | structural | Write the keys of every JSON object in reverse order; JSON objects are unordered. | `{"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1815}` -> `{"year": 1815, "ok": true, "url": "a/b", "name": "Zoë"}` | RFC 8259, misgrade design |
| `json.sort-keys` | json | answer | structural | Write the keys of every JSON object in sorted order; JSON objects are unordered. | `{"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1815}` -> `{"name": "Zoë", "ok": true, "url": "a/b", "year": 1815}` | RFC 8259, misgrade design |
| `order.factor-swap` | latex | answer | cas | Move a leading numeric coefficient to the end of its product (``2\pi`` -> ``\pi \cdot 2``); multiplication is commutative. | `2\pi` -> `\pi \cdot 2` | misgrade design |
| `order.reverse` | set | answer | structural | List the elements of the set in reverse order; a set has no order. | `{-2, 1, 3}` -> `{3, 1, -2}` | misgrade design |
| `order.rotate` | set | answer | structural | Move the first element of the set to the end; a set has no order. | `{-2, 1, 3}` -> `{1, 3, -2}` | misgrade design |
| `order.sum-swap` | latex | answer | cas | Move the first term of a sum to the end (``1 + \sqrt{2}`` -> ``\sqrt{2} + 1``); addition is commutative. | `x^2 - 1` -> `-1 + x^2` | misgrade design |
| `order.union-swap` | interval | answer | structural | List the parts of a union of intervals in reverse order; union is commutative. | `(-\infty, 0] \cup [2, \infty)` -> `[2, \infty) \cup (-\infty, 0]` | misgrade design |

## Mutants (the grader must reject)

### near-miss

| operator | types | scope | certificate | description | example (gold -> case) | motivated by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `near.change-char` | string | answer | structural | Change one letter of the text (the first vowel: ``Paris`` -> ``Peris``). | `São Paulo` -> `Sãi Paulo` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.change-element` | set | answer | structural | Add one to the last element of the set. | `{-2, 1, 3}` -> `{-2, 1, 4}` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.close-endpoint` | interval | answer | structural | Make the first open finite endpoint closed (``(1, 3)`` -> ``[1, 3)``). | `(1, 3)` -> `[1, 3)` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.digit-swap` | number | answer | cas | Swap the first two adjacent, different digits (``42`` -> ``24``). | `1250` -> `2150` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.div-ten` | number, latex | answer | cas | Divide the answer by ten (a decimal-point slip). | `1250` -> `125` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.drop-element` | set | answer | structural | Leave out the last element of the set. | `{-2, 1, 3}` -> `{-2, 1}` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.drop-pi` | latex | answer | cas | Drop the first factor ``\pi`` (``2\pi`` -> ``2``). | `2\pi` -> `2` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.drop-sqrt` | latex | answer | cas | Drop the first square root, keeping its radicand (``\sqrt{3}`` -> ``3``). | `\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}` -> `\frac{3}{2}` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.drop-union-part` | interval | answer | structural | Leave out the last interval of a union. | `(-\infty, 0] \cup [2, \infty)` -> `(-\infty, 0]` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.extra-element` | set | answer | structural | Add an element that is not in the set (one more than the largest). | `{-2, 1, 3}` -> `{-2, 1, 3, 4}` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.first-digit` | number | answer | cas | Change the first non-zero digit (1->2, ..., 9->1). | `1250` -> `2250` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.integer-part` | number | answer | cas | Keep only the integer part of a non-integer answer (``2.75`` -> ``2``). | `-2.50` -> `-2` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.json-bool` | json | answer | structural | Flip the first boolean in the JSON document. | `{"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1815}` -> `{"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": false, "year": 1815}` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.json-number` | json | answer | structural | Add one to the first number in the JSON document. | `{"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1815}` -> `{"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1816}` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.json-string` | json | answer | structural | Change one letter of the first string value in the JSON document. | `{"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1815}` -> `{"name": "Zië", "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1815}` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.latex-digit` | latex | answer | cas | Increase the first integer in the expression by one (``\frac{1}{3}`` -> ``\frac{2}{3}``). | `\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}` -> `\frac{\sqrt{4}}{2}` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.minus-one` | number, latex | answer | cas | Subtract one from the answer. | `1250` -> `1249` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.negate` | bool | answer | structural | Answer the opposite boolean, in the gold's spelling (``true`` -> ``false``). | `true` -> `false` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.next-option` | mc | answer | structural | Answer the next option instead (``B`` -> ``C``). | `B` -> `C` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.open-endpoint` | interval | answer | structural | Make the first closed finite endpoint open (``[2, \infty)`` -> ``(2, \infty)``). | `(-\infty, 0] \cup [2, \infty)` -> `(-\infty, 0) \cup [2, \infty)` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.option-text` | mc | answer | structural | Answer with the text of an adjacent option instead of a label. | `B` -> `5` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.plus-one` | number, latex | answer | cas | Add one to the answer. | `1250` -> `1251` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.prev-option` | mc | answer | structural | Answer the previous option instead (``B`` -> ``A``). | `B` -> `A` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.reciprocal` | number | answer | cas | Invert the answer (``0.5`` -> ``2``, ``42`` -> ``1/42``). | `1250` -> `0.0008` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.round` | number | answer | cas | Round the answer one place too early (``2.75`` -> ``2.8``, ``42`` -> ``40``). | `1250` -> `1300` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.shift-endpoint` | interval | answer | structural | Move the last finite endpoint outwards by one (``(1, 3)`` -> ``(1, 4)``). | `(-\infty, 0] \cup [2, \infty)` -> `(-\infty, 0] \cup [1, \infty)` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.sign-flip` | number, latex | answer | cas | Flip the sign of the answer. | `1250` -> `-1250` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.swap-chars` | string | answer | structural | Swap two adjacent, different characters of the text (``Paris`` -> ``Prais``). | `São Paulo` -> `Soã Paulo` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.swap-frac` | latex | answer | cas | Swap the numerator and denominator of the first fraction. | `\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}` -> `\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `near.times-ten` | number, latex | answer | cas | Multiply the answer by ten (a decimal-point slip). | `1250` -> `12500` | arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |

| `jsonstruct.array-wrap` | json | answer | structural | Put the document inside a one-element array. | `{"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1815}` -> `[{"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1815}]` | misgrade design |
| `jsonstruct.duplicate-key` | json | answer | structural | Repeat the last key of the object with a wrong value; ECMAScript ``JSON.parse`` and Python's ``json`` keep the last value. | `{"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1815}` -> `{"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1815, "year": 1816}` | RFC 8259, arXiv:2605.02909, misgrade design |
| `jsonstruct.extra-field` | json | answer | structural | Add a field the gold does not have (``"extra": null``), or an extra array element. | `{"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1815}` -> `{"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1815, "extra": null}` | misgrade design |
| `jsonstruct.missing-field` | json | answer | structural | Leave out the last field of the object (or the last array element). | `{"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1815}` -> `{"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": true}` | misgrade design |
| `jsonstruct.null-field` | json | answer | structural | Set the first non-null field of the object to ``null``. | `{"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1815}` -> `{"name": null, "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1815}` | misgrade design |
| `jsonstruct.wrap` | json | answer | structural | Nest the document one level down under a ``"result"`` key. | `{"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1815}` -> `{"result": {"name": "Zoë", "url": "a/b", "ok": true, "year": 1815}}` | misgrade design |

## References

- **arXiv:2609.01354**: reports 53.8-95.2% self-validation for four widely used verifiers on identical inputs, 49.9% disagreement between two configurations of one library, and whitespace/punctuation behind 93% of in-contract failures. <https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.01354>
- **arXiv:2605.02909**: reports that the pattern of false positives, not their rate, decides whether RLVR training plateaus or collapses, and that mitigating them before training is hard. <https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.02909>
- **arXiv:2507.08794**: content-free 'master key' responses (':', 'Thought process:', 'Solution', '解', ...) that LLM judges accept. <https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.08794>
- **verl#8011**: after one math_verify worker dies, every later correct answer scores 0. <https://github.com/volcengine/verl/issues/8011>
- **Math-Verify#79**: Math-Verify's timeouts do not work on Windows. <https://github.com/huggingface/Math-Verify/issues/79>
- **lm-evaluation-harness#4230**: a multiple-choice regex read the response 'Note: All ...' as option A. <https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness/issues/4230>
- **openai/simple-evals**: asks the model to end with a line 'Answer: X'. <https://github.com/openai/simple-evals>
- **lm-eval minerva_math**: expects 'Final Answer: The final answer is X. I hope it is correct.'. <https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness/tree/main/lm_eval/tasks/minerva_math>
- **RFC 8259**: JSON: whitespace is insignificant around structural characters, any character may be escaped, objects are unordered, names SHOULD be unique. <https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259>
- **Unicode UAX #15**: canonical (NFC/NFD) and compatibility (NFKC) equivalence of Unicode text. <https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr15/>
- **SI Brochure**: digits may be grouped in threes, separated by a (thin) space. <https://www.bipm.org/en/publications/si-brochure>
- **amsmath**: defines \dfrac and \tfrac as \frac in display and text style. <https://ctan.org/pkg/amsmath>
- **The TeXbook**: an undelimited macro argument is a single token or a {group}; spaces in math mode are ignored.
- **misgrade design**: the operator families misgrade certifies (docs/design.md, section 1). ([design.md](design.md))
